record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Can the known geometric condition guaranteeing efficient sampling of lattice points in a convex body be weakened substantially? In particular, can one sample lattice points efficiently from a near-isotropic convex body, or from a convex body that contains at least half of a Euclidean ball of radius O(sqrt(n))?

evidence.quote: Can this condition be improved substantially? E.g., can one sample lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body? Or lattice points of a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(√n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called isotropic if its centroid is at the origin and $\int_K xx^\top\,dx/\mathrm{vol}(K) = I_n$; it is near-isotropic if this covariance matrix is within a constant factor of the identity in the Loewner order. For an integer $t\geq 1$, $K$ is said to contain a fraction of a Euclidean ball if it contains at least half of $B(0,r)$ for some specified radius $r$. A lattice-point sampler for $K$ with respect to the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$ is a randomized algorithm that, given a suitable oracle access to $K$ (e.g., a membership oracle), outputs a random point of $K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$ whose distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on $K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$, using time and oracle calls polynomial in $n$ and $\log(1/\varepsilon)$.

It is known that one can sample efficiently from $K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$ under a relatively strong geometric condition on $K$ (such as $K$ containing a Euclidean ball of radius polynomial in $n$ that is large compared with $\sqrt{n}$).

Question. Can this geometric requirement be substantially weakened? Concretely:

(a) Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a near-isotropic convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ via a membership oracle, samples (approximately uniformly) from $K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$?

(b) Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ which contains at least half of a Euclidean ball of radius $O(\sqrt{n})$, samples (approximately uniformly) from $K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaced ongoing work on sampling from continuous convex bodies in (near-)isotropic position, but no source was found establishing or refuting a polynomial-time algorithm for sampling lattice points from a near-isotropic convex body or from a body containing half of a ball of radius O(√n). The status of these specific questions appears unresolved in the surveyed literature.

status_evidence.title: High-dimensional Sampling Algorithms (Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of sampling algorithms for convex bodies in (near-)isotropic position; lattice-point sampling under weakened geometric conditions is not established.
status_evidence.claim: No general polynomial-time lattice-point sampler for near-isotropic convex bodies is reported.

status_evidence.title: Faster Polytope Rounding, Sampling, and Volume Computation
status_evidence.snippet: Recent advances on continuous sampling for near-isotropic bodies; does not address discrete (lattice) sampling under the relaxed conditions in question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress concerns continuous sampling, not the lattice-point version asked here.
